points.description: Identifies abstraction as a main advantage of object-oriented programming. Equivalent wording earns the mark, for example hiding complex internal detail behind a simpler interface or representing only the essential features of an object.

Identifies reusability as a main advantage of object-oriented programming. Equivalent wording earns the mark, for example reusing classes or objects in other programs or parts of a program, or reusing code through inheritance.

rubric.notes: The model answer names two advantages, so the 5 marks split equally between them. A student earns full marks for naming both abstraction and reusability, using equivalent wording or a clear explanation of each. A student who names only one of the two earns 2.5 marks, and a student who names neither earns no marks.
